# Philippa Gordon

## Overview

- **Age:** Early twenties  <sub>[v3 c4 P46](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0046), [v3 c4 P56](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0056), [v3 c35 P0](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0000)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c4 P22](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0022)</sub>
- **Status:** Married  <sub>[v3 c39 P39](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0039)</sub>
- **Origin:** Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia  <sub>[v3 c4 P32](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0032), [v3 c4 P44](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0044)</sub>
- **Role:** Student (formerly), Minister's wife  <sub>[v3 c24 P21](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0021), [v3 c27 P29](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0029), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Phil  <sub>[v3 c4 P28](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0028)</sub>; Philippa  <sub>[v3 c4 P28](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0028)</sub>

## Appearance

Philippa is a strikingly beautiful girl with brown, velvety eyes, dark-pointed black brows, a rose-red crooked mouth, and a rose-ripe glow on her round cheeks. She has a satin-smooth head of hair with brown nut tints. As a Redmond student, she is renowned as the class beauty and dresses in stylish, high-fashioned clothes.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P22](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0022), [v3 c4 P36](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0036), [v3 c5 P6](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0006), [v3 c26 P1](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0001)_

## Personality

Philippa is gay, irrepressible, and intensely charming, possessing a whimsical and volatile nature. Though she appears shallow, frivolous, and indecisive on the surface, she is fiercely loyal, generous, and has a deep, womanly heart. She is candidly aware of her own beauty and popularity, enjoying the admiration of many suitors without malice. Despite her luxurious upbringing, she is cheerful and willing to adapt to a simpler, poorer lifestyle for the sake of true love.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P26](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0026), [v3 c4 P40](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0040), [v3 c4 P61](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0061), [v3 c5 P2](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0002), [v3 c20 P7](../source/v03-c20.md#nw-v03-c20-p0007), [v3 c27 P21](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0021), [v3 c27 P31](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0031)_

## History

Philippa Gordon first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John’s Cemetery during their Freshman year at Redmond College. She quickly formed an intense friendship with them, introducing them into Redmond's social life. During her college years, she lived with Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard at Patty’s Place under the care of Aunt Jamesina. While at a summer boardinghouse at Prospect Point, she met Jonas Blake, a poor divinity student, and fell deeply in love with him, discarding her former wealthy suitors, Alec and Alonzo. She graduated from Redmond with Honors in Mathematics to prove her intellect to Jonas. In her graduate year, Jonas proposed to her and she accepted. Following her graduation, Philippa married Jonas in Bolingbroke and moved with him to work in the slums of Patterson Street.

_Sources: [v3 c4 P24](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0024), [v3 c5 P2](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0002), [v3 c10 P48](../source/v03-c10.md#nw-v03-c10-p0048), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c24 P8](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0008), [v3 c27 P17](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0017), [v3 c27 P29](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0029), [v3 c35 P5](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0005), [v3 c39 P39](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0039), [v3 c39 P40](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0040)_

## Quotes

> I can’t decide even on my own appearance. Just as soon as I’ve decided that I’m pretty I begin to feel miserably that I’m not.  <sub>[v3 c4 P40](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0040)</sub>

> I was born a see-saw Aunty, and nothing can ever prevent me from teetering.  <sub>[v3 c19 P23](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0023)</sub>

> It’s a very old-fashioned way. But I am old-fashioned. My clothes are, and it stands to reason my opinions are, too.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> I shall be poor as gaily as I’ve been rich. You’ll see. I’m going to learn how to cook and make over dresses.  <sub>[v3 c27 P31](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0031)</sub>

> I didn’t say I’d like to break it. I said I’d like to think I could break it. I would like to know I had the power to do it.  <sub>[v3 c25 P21](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0021)</sub>
